title: Real Estate Service Contracts Failed-Sale Charge Amount
content:
**Clause.** The failed-sale charge on a Real Estate Service Contracts listing order is worked out from the order's own billing and claim records, as follows.

(a) The plan premium invoiced is the sum of the plan invoices on the order; every plan invoice posted on the order counts toward it.

(b) The seller-phase benefit paid is the sum of the benefit authorizations on the order less the authorization reversals on it, rounded to the cent.

(c) The failed-sale charge cap is the plan premium invoiced.

(d) The failed-sale charge is the lesser of the failed-sale charge cap and the seller-phase benefit paid, never below zero, rounded to the cent.

(e) No failed-sale charge is billed when the seller-phase benefit paid is zero, and seller service call fees already collected never reduce it.

## Inputs and the records they come from

| Quantity | Record |
|---|---|
| Plan premium invoiced | the plan invoices in the order's billing history |
| Benefit authorizations | the benefit authorizations in the order's claim records |
| Authorization reversals | the authorization reversals in the order's claim records |

## Worked examples (hypothetical orders)

1. One plan invoice of $650.00. Benefit authorizations of $900.00 and $300.00, and one reversal of $300.00. Seller-phase benefit paid: $1200.00 less $300.00, which is $900.00. The cap is $650.00. The failed-sale charge is the lesser of $650.00 and $900.00: **$650.00**.
2. One plan invoice of $545.00. One benefit authorization of $420.00 and no reversal. The failed-sale charge is the lesser of $545.00 and $420.00: **$420.00**.
3. One plan invoice of $795.00 and no benefit authorization, while the seller paid two service call fees during the listing: the seller-phase benefit paid is zero, so **no failed-sale charge** is billed; the service call fees play no part.
4. As in example 2, with $85.00 of seller service call fees already collected: the charge remains **$420.00**; collected fees never reduce it.
